root_idea.summary: A root centered on accumulated bodily dirt and unkemptness, especially the condition produced by suspended grooming.
root_idea.development: The lexical development extends from dirt on the nails and body, and matted or dusty hair, to the pilgrimage expression قضاء التفث: removing that condition through cleansing, grooming, and related acts of release from ihram restrictions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested nominal is presented under the normalized citation form تَفَثٌ.

senses.definition: Accumulated bodily dirt and unkemptness, including matted or dusty hair and neglected bodily grooming.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic pilgrimage context, this is the condition to be removed after the period of ihram-related grooming restrictions; the term can also denote bodily dirt more generally.

senses.definition: The cleansing and grooming acts that remove pilgrimage-related unkemptness and complete the transition out of ihram.
senses.usage_conditions: Used especially in the construction قضاء التفث. Explanations include shaving or shortening hair, trimming the moustache, paring the nails, removing unwanted hair, and related acts; some explanations extend it to associated pilgrimage rites and release from ihram restrictions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dirty or unkempt after leaving off anointing oneself and grooming the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; the described condition includes neglected anointing and shaving or other grooming, particularly in the pilgrimage setting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dusty, matted-haired, and altered in odour; unkempt from lack of anointing and grooming.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of a person or one exhibiting this unkempt condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contaminate or soil a place, as blood does in the cited expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested as a reported idiomatic expression and distinct from the pilgrimage-related dirt and cleansing usage.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers the dirty or unkempt condition, its removal in the pilgrimage construction, and the related Form I verb.
Reports the distinct contaminating expression involving blood and a place.
Covers the adjectival sense of dusty, matted, and unkempt.

cautions: The single Quran occurrence is in قضاء التفث. Classical explanations differ over whether the expression emphasizes the dirt or unkempt condition itself, the grooming acts that remove it, or a wider set of pilgrimage completion rites.
